Assistant A provides a more structured and detailed breakdown of how each life stage (childhood, adolescence/young adulthood, middle age, old age) distinctly shapes perceptions of time and mortality. Assistant B offers a more general narrative with only two broad phases (“when we are young” and “as we get older”) and less specific insight into the nuances of each stage. Therefore, Assistant A’s response is more helpful, relevant, and detailed.
